exact_scope: WP715 packet-cortex SESSION_CLOSE atomicity and active-tool terminalization only

reproduced_negatives.finding: A rejected SESSION_CLOSE changes the exported recoverable checkpoint; commit-eligible output receives a voiceoutcome_ref before the later SESSION_CLOSE event validation rejects the close.
reproduced_negatives.root_cause: close_session creates VoiceOutcome and mutates commit-eligible outputs before _event validates/constructs the SESSION_CLOSE event. A late validation error therefore leaves partial mutation behind.

reproduced_negatives.finding: A successful SESSION_CLOSE removes an active tool from ownership without preserving a cancelled/stale tombstone and without a causal terminalization event.
reproduced_negatives.root_cause: close_session ends with _active_tools.clear() and does not transfer active tool refs into _cancelled_tools or emit an explicit tool-fence/cancellation event.

repair_contract: Prevalidate the complete close transaction before mutating outputs, tool ownership, event sequence, or closed state; any rejected close must be checkpoint-identical to pre-call state.
For active tools at successful close, either fail closed without mutation or terminalize every owned tool explicitly with durable stale/cancelled fencing and causal event evidence before closure.
Reserve/validate all event capacity and event fields needed by the close transaction before the first mutation.
Keep the two landed regression tests; add no broader voice architecture while closing this defect.

runtime_subject_fence.instruction: Do not derive current repaired runtime credit from the old queued subject. Repair under the existing WP715 Trigger4 owner, rerun exact-source repository CI, then bind one new exact repaired subject to VPS only after the repair is green.

next_exact_action: Existing F2-WP-715 Trigger4 mutation owner applies one coherent SESSION_CLOSE transaction repair for both reproduced defects, reruns the exact two regressions plus the full WP715 packet/recovery suite, classifies any remaining failures, and only then rebinds an exact repaired VPS discriminator.
